target_customer: Enterprises and regulated users needing auditable AI models
problem: Large language models are opaque; users cannot trace outputs to training data or concepts.
business_model: Models and agents, possibly API/enterprise (not sourced)

founders.name: Julius Adebayo
education: PhD, MIT (company page says team has PhDs from MIT, UMD, MILA; individual not attributed)
founders.background_notes: Machine learning researcher in interpretability per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building interpretable foundation models is research-grade; the company says it built the first interpretable diffusion model and LLM.

defensibility.rationale: Research talent and a model line others do not have, but unproven commercially.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large labs had interpretability research efforts but were not shipping inherently interpretable models as products; not verified with a dated source.

market_need_then: Regulation and enterprise caution about black-box AI created demand for auditing, per the company's positioning; no data read.

identity.logo: ten purple slits oriented in a circle (company site)

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand evidence beyond the logo.

outcome_analysis: Guide Labs is an active Winter 2024 research-heavy company that released Steerling-8B, described as the largest inherently interpretable model, and open-sourced it in February 2026 per the YC page. Investors listed include Initialized, Tectonic, Lombardstreet, Pioneer and E14, but no amounts were found; commercial traction is unknown, so the outcome is still open.
